root_idea.summary: A root centered on decisive resolve: fixing an affair firmly in the mind and cutting off hesitation.
root_idea.development: The semantic range develops from decisive settlement or severance to resolving and carrying out an affair, steadfastly pursuing a course, and related notions of endurance, earnest command, and conjuring.

senses.definition: To resolve, decide, or determine firmly to carry out an affair.
senses.usage_conditions: Used with عَلَى or عَلَيْهِ and also with a direct object. With an affair as subject, the related construction expresses that the affair has become settled or serious; that construction is listed separately.

senses.definition: Of an affair, to become determined or settled; to become serious or earnest.
senses.usage_conditions: A conventional intransitive construction, عَزَمَ الأَمْرُ, in which the affair itself is presented as determined or serious.

senses.definition: Firm resolve or determination to carry out an affair; a fixed purpose of the mind.
senses.usage_conditions: Occurs in expressions such as عَزْمِ الأُمُورِ, “matters requiring firm resolve,” and may denote maintaining what has been commanded while intending to perform it.

senses.definition: Steadfastness, constancy, and patience in carrying out an obligation or enduring a matter.
senses.usage_conditions: Especially associated with أُولُو العَزْمِ مِنَ الرُّسُلِ, the messengers marked by resoluteness, constancy, and patience.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To strive, labor, toil, or exert one's efforts in an affair.
To conjure or earnestly command or enjoin someone to do something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction عَزَمَ عَلَى الرَّجُلِ takes the person addressed as its object and conveys an earnest demand with no exception.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To recite charms or spells, as a charmer does.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a charmer or serpent-charmer reciting charms for a disease or to draw out a serpent.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To invite someone to an entertainment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A later usage reported as current in Lane’s description.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To go or tend toward a place.
To keep to a course, especially to go along a road without turning aside.
To tend, betake oneself, or repair to someone or something, directly or indirectly.
Of a horse, to run forcefully, overcoming its rider’s attempts to check or turn it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a horse that continues its run without complying with the rider’s effort to restrain it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To bear or endure something or someone patiently.
The dregs of pressed raisins.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural is reported as عُزُمٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A vulgar expression for the anus.
Striving, labor, toil, or strength in an affair.
Determination, a deliberate way of proceeding, or steadfastness and patience in what one undertakes.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a person’s ability to remain constant and steady in an affair once undertaken.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An obligatory due or statute imposed by God.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression عَزْمَةٌ مِنْ عَزَمَاتِ الله denotes a divinely imposed obligation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A man’s near paternal kin or tribe.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural is reported as عُزَمٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A man who fulfills his promises.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to one who performs what he promises.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A seller of the dregs of pressed raisins.
A resolute person who perseveres in determination until attaining what he seeks.
Vehement or forceful running.
An obligatory statute or ordinance of God.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural عَزَائِمُ الله denotes God’s obligatory ordinances.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A charm or spell; also, a Quranic passage recited over an afflicted person in hope of healing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural عَزَائِمُ may denote charms recited to conjure jinn or spirits, and عَزَائِمُ القُرْآنِ denotes Quranic verses used in such recitation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A designated Quranic passage of prostration.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In the plural expression عَزَائِمُ السُّجُودِ, it refers to portions of the Quran in whose recitation prostration is commanded.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The lion.
A resolute person, especially one steadfast or true in love or affection.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The related plural may also be applied to affairs characterized by firm determination and fulfillment of what God has enjoined.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An extremely old she-camel, sometimes retaining some youthful vigor.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term is also applied in an extended use to an old woman.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Short, as an epithet applied to a woman.
A charmer who uses spells.
